values.goal: Design Canvas ownership and size·input protocols, and evaluate the benefits and costs of Worker rendering.
values.capstone: Run the same particle scene on the main thread and in a Worker, comparing resize·input·errors·stop·restart behavior.

values.title: Transferring Canvas Control
values.prerequisites: Understand Canvas 2D·Web Workers, and be able to read the inputs and outputs of the existing starting examples.
values.environment: The existing offscreen-canvas-01·02·03 are starting examples for supported browsers. Implement the new units in main-thread and Worker files in a separate local HTTP project. Check API and context support, and provide a main-thread fallback on a new Canvas if transfer fails. Preserve CSP and isolation, and record performance measurements yourself.
values.concepts.0.title: Ownership
values.concepts.0.explanation: transferControlToOffscreen transfers control of the display Canvas. Do not create a rendering context on the same Canvas before transferring it.
values.concepts.1.title: Fallback path
values.concepts.1.explanation: API support and successful initialization are different. On failure, recover with main-thread rendering on a new Canvas.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Ownership. Input cases: Supported and forced-unsupported paths.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: A table of the selected mode, first frame, and error guidance. Explain the rationale for handling Fallback path, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In src/day-1.js in a separate practice project, check feature support, transfer the OffscreenCanvas to a Worker, and implement a main-thread fallback. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: Supported and forced-unsupported paths. Baseline: Supported. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-1.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: Support flag; changed value: Force unsupported. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: A table of the selected mode, first frame, and error guidance. Hypothesis to check: Main-thread rendering or clear guidance appears instead of a blank screen. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.
values.variables.0.name: Support flag
values.variables.0.expected: Main-thread rendering or clear guidance appears instead of a blank screen.
values.criteria.0: Required deliverable: A table of the selected mode, first frame, and error guidance. Results are available for both the baseline and changed conditions, allowing comparison of 2 conditions; input values and the execution environment are recorded together.
values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: Ownership and Fallback path. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Ownership affect in this exercise? Input cases: Supported and forced-unsupported paths.
values.questions.1: Variable: Support flag. Hypothesis to check: Main-thread rendering or clear guidance appears instead of a blank screen. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Fallback path.

values.references.1.title: MDN Using Web Workers

values.concepts.0.title: Pure state
values.concepts.0.explanation: The renderer draws from the state it receives rather than from the DOM. The same draw function can run in different execution contexts.
values.concepts.1.title: Ownership boundaries
values.concepts.1.explanation: The main thread manages the DOM and input. The Worker manages the Canvas and scene state.

values.steps.2: Variable: Execution context; changed value: Worker. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: A table of coordinates and colors for both adapters. values.concepts.0.title: Ready
values.concepts.0.explanation: Input sent immediately after transferring the Canvas may arrive before initialization finishes. A ready response signals readiness.
values.concepts.1.title: Pending input
values.concepts.1.explanation: Hold input until ready, or retain only its latest value. An indefinite wait needs an error path.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Ready. Input cases: A color change immediately after initialization.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: Message order and the first applied color. Explain the rationale for handling Pending input, linking it to the code.

values.steps.1: Input conditions: A color change immediately after initialization. Baseline: After ready. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-3.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: Input timing; changed value: Before ready. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: Message order and the first applied color. Hypothesis to check: The latest input is applied once initialization is ready. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.

values.variables.0.expected: The latest input is applied once initialization is ready.
values.criteria.0: Required deliverable: Message order and the first applied color. Results are available for both the baseline and changed conditions, allowing comparison of 2 conditions; input values and the execution environment are recorded together.
values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: Ready and Pending input. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Ready affect in this exercise? Input cases: A color change immediately after initialization.
values.questions.1: Variable: Input timing. Hypothesis to check: The latest input is applied once initialization is ready. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Pending input.

values.concepts.0.explanation: CSS size determines the layout on screen. It differs from the size of the pixel backing store.
values.concepts.1.title: DPR
values.concepts.1.explanation: DPR is the ratio of backing-store pixels to CSS pixels. Rendering and input must use the same units.
